1: At Gibeon God offers Solomon whatever he wants. He asks for wisdom to lead the people and receives wealth and honour too.
2: Solomon asks Hiram of Tyre for cedar and a master craftsman, and organises the workforce.
"Who is able to build him a house, since heaven cannot contain him?"
3: Solomon starts building on Mount Moriah, where Abraham had offered Isaac, and overlays the inner room with gold.
The Temple stands on ground already marked by sacrifice.
4: The bronze altar, the great basin, lampstands, tables and vessels are made.
Everything in God's house is made with care.
5: The priests set the ark in the Holy of Holies. As the singers praise God, a cloud fills the Temple.
God's presence answers his people's praise.
6: Solomon kneels and asks God to hear every prayer made toward this house: for forgiveness, rain, victory, and for the foreigner.
The Temple is meant as a place of mercy for all.
7: Fire consumes the sacrifices and glory fills the house. God promises, "If my people humble themselves, pray, seek my face and turn from their wicked ways, I will forgive."
That promise of forgiveness is the heart of the book.
8: Solomon builds cities, organises labour and keeps the appointed sacrifices.
The worship David planned is carried out.
9: The queen tests Solomon and praises God for him. His wealth is described. Solomon dies.
The nations are drawn by the wisdom God gives.
10: Rehoboam rejects the elders' advice and answers harshly. Ten tribes leave.
Pride splits what David and Solomon built.
11: God forbids civil war. Priests and faithful Israelites from the north move to Judah.
People leave home to be able to worship rightly.
12: Rehoboam abandons the law, and Shishak of Egypt attacks. The king and leaders humble themselves, and God limits the damage.
13: Outnumbered two to one, King Abijah declares that Judah has kept the true priesthood. Judah cries to the Lord and wins.
"They relied on the Lord, the God of their fathers."
14: Asa removes foreign altars. When a huge army attacks, he prays, "Lord, there is none like you to help the weak," and wins.
Numbers do not decide the battle.
15: A prophet tells Asa, "The Lord is with you while you are with him." Asa clears out idols and the people renew the covenant with joy.
16: Threatened by Israel, Asa buys help from Syria instead of trusting God. Rebuked, he jails the prophet. In illness he looks only to physicians.
A good start is not enough. "The eyes of the Lord search the whole earth to strengthen those whose heart is his."
17: Jehoshaphat sends officials and Levites through Judah to teach the people from the book of the law.
18: Jehoshaphat allies with Ahab. Micaiah alone foretells defeat. Ahab dies in battle, and Jehoshaphat barely escapes.
A bad alliance puts a good man in danger.
19: A prophet rebukes the alliance. Jehoshaphat appoints judges and tells them, "You judge not for man but for the Lord."
20: A vast enemy comes. Jehoshaphat prays, "We do not know what to do, but our eyes are on you." Singers go out in front, and the enemies destroy each other.
"The battle is not yours but God's."
21: Jehoram murders his brothers and follows Ahab's ways. He dies of a painful disease, and no one regrets him.
Marrying into Ahab's family brought his sins into Judah.
22: Ahaziah reigns one year and is killed. His mother Athaliah seizes the throne and kills the royal children, but baby Joash is hidden.
23: The priest Jehoiada crowns the seven-year-old Joash in the Temple. Athaliah is put to death and Baal's temple torn down.
A faithful priest saves the kingdom.
24: Joash repairs the Temple while Jehoiada lives. Afterwards he turns to idols and has Jehoiada's son Zechariah stoned.
Borrowed faith fails when the mentor is gone.
25: Amaziah obeys a prophet and wins a battle, then worships the gods of the people he defeated and is beaten by Israel.
26: Uzziah prospers as long as he seeks God. Grown powerful, he enters the Temple to burn incense, which only priests may do, and is struck with leprosy.
Success leads to pride, and pride to a fall.
27: Jotham does right, builds, and grows strong.
"He ordered his ways before the Lord his God."
28: Ahaz worships idols, sacrifices his sons, is defeated on every side and shuts the Temple doors.
Trouble makes him worse instead of turning him back.
29: In his first month Hezekiah opens and cleanses the Temple and restores sacrifice and song.
30: Hezekiah invites all Israel, north and south, to keep Passover. Many mock, some come. God pardons those not ritually ready.
God looks at the heart that seeks him.
31: The people destroy idols and bring so many offerings that they are piled in heaps.
32: Assyria invades. Hezekiah encourages the people: "With him is an arm of flesh; with us is the Lord." An angel destroys the invaders.
Hezekiah later struggles with pride and humbles himself.
33: Manasseh does great evil. Taken captive in chains, he humbles himself and prays, and God brings him back. He then removes the idols.
No one is beyond God's mercy.
34: Josiah begins seeking God at sixteen. The book of the law is found during repairs, and he leads the people in renewing the covenant.
A young person can lead a nation back to God.
35: Josiah keeps the greatest Passover since Samuel. He later dies fighting Pharaoh Neco.
36: The last four kings fail. God sends messengers again and again until there is no remedy. Jerusalem is destroyed. Seventy years later Cyrus of Persia invites the exiles home.
The book ends with an open door.
